title: Cellular RNA G-quadruplex Profiling Using G4RP.v2
author: Mitteaux, Monchaud

CRITICAL: Prepare all reagents (or at least the final buffers and solutions) in a sterile environment (e.g., under a standard biosafety cabinet, with 0.2-μm filtration, etc.).

The analysis of the qPCR data is performed according to the following steps: i- set the threshold for the SYBR Green fluorescence intensity (FI), ii- recover the Ct (dR) values, iii- normalize the Ct (dR) values using the G4RP-RT-qPCR signal formula, as follows.1.Set the FI threshold:a.The thermocycler (Agilent) displays the amplification curves on a y = f(x)-type graph with the following parameters: baseline-corrected raw SYBR Green FI (dR) on cycles number (cycles).b.Put the dR in log(y).c.Focus only in the almost-vertical and parallel part of exponential curves and select the lowest FI validating these two last prerequisites (= the inflection point) to place the threshold horizontal line.2.Recover the Ct (dR) values:a.Put the dR back in linear y.b.Take the cycle number corresponding to the intersection point between the previous threshold FI horizontal line and the appropriate amplification curve corresponding to an experimental condition = this is the Ct (dR) value of your experimental condition.3.Normalize the Ct (dR) values:a.Calculate the “Mean Ct input” which is the mean of Ct (dR) values for the 5% input control (biological triplicate).b.Calculate the G4RP-RT-qPCR signal = 5∗(2(Mean Ct input) – Ct G4RP or biotin), with each technical Ct (dR) of G4RP (= G4-precipitation with TASQ) or biotin experimental condition.c.For each precipitation and target condition (e.g., NRAS G4 precipitation with BioCyTASQ, VEGFA G4 precipitation with biotin control):i.Calculate the technical mean G4RP-RT-qPCR signal for each biological replicate (with the technical replicates).ii.Calculate the mean of G4RP-RT-qPCR signal (with the biological replicates).d.Make your data representation with these mean normalized values.e.Analyze your data (see problems 7, 8, and 9, troubleshooting section).

steps.title: Clean benchtops and materials
steps.instruction: Wipe all benchtops (including fume‑hood work surfaces) and all reusable labware (pipettes, racks, etc.) with RNaseZap to eliminate RNase contamination.

steps.title: Thaw, plate and grow MCF7 cells
steps.instruction: Thaw a frozen MCF7 vial, add supplemented DMEM, plate in a suitable culture flask, and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. The next morning replace the medium with fresh supplemented DMEM to remove DMSO from the stock.

steps.title: Passage MCF7 cells as needed
steps.instruction: When confluence is reached, remove medium, wash cells with sterile 1 X PBS, add trypsin, incubate 37 °C for 3–5 min, check detachment, neutralize with an equal volume of supplemented DMEM, reseed at the desired density in fresh medium and return to the incubator.

steps.title: Prepare denaturing agarose gel (optional)
steps.instruction: Cast a denaturing agarose gel (0.026 % w/v bleach, 1.5 % w/v agarose) and store immersed in 1 X TBE at 4 °C for up to 3–4 days if not used immediately.

steps.title: Prepare G4‑interacting agents and TASQs
steps.instruction: Make 2 mM BRACO‑19 (stock in DMSO) and 20 mM PhpC (stock in ddH₂O). Prepare 1 mM solutions of BioTASQ, BioCyTASQ and/or azMultiTASQ, and a solution of biotin‑PEG(4)‑DBCO for the click reaction. Verify the click reaction (azMultiTASQ + biotin‑PEG(4)‑DBCO, 37 °C, 1 h, agitation) by HPLC‑MS; this analysis is mandatory.

steps.title: Select RT and qPCR programs
steps.instruction:
Load the following programs on the Agilent MX3005P (or equivalent):
• RT: 5 min @ 25 °C, 45 min @ 55 °C, 15 min @ 70 °C, 10 min @ 25 °C (total 75 min).
• qPCR amplification: 10 min @ 95 °C, then 60 cycles of 30 s @ 95 °C, 45 s @ 60 °C, 45 s @ 72 °C (total 130 min). Optional reduction to 35 cycles.
• qPCR dissociation: 1 min @ 95 °C, 30 s @ 55 °C, 30 s @ 95 °C, 30 s @ 55 °C, 30 s @ 95 °C (2 min 30 s).

steps.title: Prepare qPCR primer couples
steps.instruction: Resuspend and dilute the primer pairs for NRAS and VEGFA (or any other targets) in UltraPure DNase/RNase‑free distilled water; keep all primers on ice.

steps.title: Prepare all buffers and solutions
steps.instruction:
Make the following reagents (using RNase‑free water and sterile technique):
• Biotin 1 mM and 10 mM
• BRACO‑19 2 mM (stock)
• DEPC‑H₂O 0.1 % v/v
• EDTA 0.5 M, pH 8.0
• EGTA 0.5 M, pH 8.0
• Fixing buffer 5X
• G4RP buffer pH 7.4
• Glycine 1 M
• HCl 1 M
• HEPES‑KOH 1 M, pH 7.5
• KCl 1 M, KOH 1 M, NaCl 1 M, NaOH 1 M
• PhpC 20 mM (stock)
• SDS 20 % w/v
• Supplemented DMEM culture medium
• TBE 10X pH 8.3 and 1X TBE.
Store all solutions at appropriate temperatures and keep them RNase‑free.

steps.title: Prepare RNA Clean‑&‑Concentrator‑5 kit reagents
steps.instruction: Reconstitute DNase I to ~1 U/µL and prepare the RNA Wash Buffer according to the kit instructions; keep everything RNase‑free.

steps.title: Seed cells for treatment (Day 1)
steps.instruction: In a 175 cm² flask add 7 × 10⁶ exponentially growing MCF7 cells in 8 mL supplemented DMEM. Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Prepare a parallel flask for each condition (control, BRACO‑19, PhpC) and optionally a fourth flask for cell counting only.

steps.title: Add G4‑interacting agents (Day 2)
steps.instruction:
Remove the medium from each flask and add 8 mL fresh medium containing the appropriate agent:
• Control: 33.7 µL DMSO (≈0.4 % v/v).
• BRACO‑19: 33.7 µL of 2 mM BRACO‑19 (final 8.42 µM, ≈5 µg/mL) + DMSO to reach 0.4 % v/v.
• PhpC: 36 µL of 20 mM PhpC + 33.7 µL DMSO (final 90 µM, DMSO 0.4 % v/v).
Homogenize gently, return the medium to the corresponding flask and incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Lyse cells and add TRIzol (Day 4 morning)
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL TRIzol to each tube containing the harvested cells (or to the cell pellet after lysis) as quickly as possible, mix gently, then immediately snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen for 1 min and store at –80 °C (overnight).

steps.title: Thaw and phase‑separate RNA
steps.instruction: Thaw samples for 5–6 min at 27 °C on a heating block with gentle stirring, then let stand 5 min at room temperature. Add 0.2 mL chloroform, seal tightly, shake vigorously 15 s, incubate 3 min at room temperature, and centrifuge 12 000 rpm (13 680 g) for 15 min at 4 °C. Transfer the clear aqueous phase (~600 µL) to a new RNase‑free tube.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of absolute ethanol to the aqueous phase (1:1), invert gently to mix.

steps.title: Purify RNA on Zymo‑Spin IC columns
steps.instruction: Load the ethanol‑mixed sample onto a Zymo‑Spin IC column placed in a collection tube and centrifuge 12 000 rpm for 30 s; discard flow‑through. Wash with 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer, centrifuge 30 s, discard. Prepare DNase I mix (5 µL DNase I (~1 U/µL) + 35 µL DNA Digestion Buffer), add 40 µL to the column matrix, incubate 15 min at room temperature. Continue washing: 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer, 30 s spin; 700 µL RNA Wash Buffer, 30 s spin; 400 µL RNA Wash Buffer, 30 s spin (repeat twice to ensure complete removal). Transfer column to a fresh 1.5 mL RNase‑free tube, elute RNA by adding 15 µL RNase‑free water, incubate 2 min, centrifuge 30 s; repeat elution with another 15 µL water (total eluate ≈30 µL). Incubate eluate 15 min at 55 °C to resolubilize RNA, keep on ice.

steps.title: Measure RNA concentration by UV absorbance
steps.instruction: Set a baseline using the appropriate buffer (G4RP lysis buffer for raw lysate, RNase‑free water for purified RNA). Measure absorbance from 200‑340 nm, record A230, A260, A270, A280. Calculate ratios R1 = A260/A230, R2 = A260/A270, R3 = A260/A280 and estimate RNA concentration as A260 × 40 ng/µL. Use RNase‑free water for dilutions; clean cuvette between samples.

steps.title: Run denaturing agarose gel (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.026 % (w/v) bleach, 1.5 % (w/v) agarose gel, submerge in 1 X TBE. Mix each sample with 0.5 µL 2X loading dye, incubate 10 min at 70 °C, then chill on ice 5–10 min. Load 4 µL sample and 2 µL RNA ladder per well. Run at 100 V (≈12 W) for 1.75 h at 4 °C. Stain by immersing gel in 7.5 µL SYBR Gold (10 000X) diluted in 75 mL 1 X TBE for 20 min at room temperature in the dark, then image.

steps.title: Perform reverse transcription
steps.instruction: Using the prepared RT program, combine RNA with reverse‑transcriptase mix (SuperScript III) as per kit instructions and run 75 min program (5 min @ 25 °C, 45 min @ 55 °C, 15 min @ 70 °C, 10 min @ 25 °C) to generate cDNA.

steps.title: Run quantitative PCR
steps.instruction: Set up qPCR reactions with the cDNA, primers, and SYBR Green master mix. Run the amplification program (10 min @ 95 °C, then 60 cycles of 30 s @ 95 °C, 45 s @ 60 °C, 45 s @ 72 °C) followed by the dissociation program (1 min @ 95 °C, 30 s @ 55 °C, 30 s @ 95 °C, 30 s @ 55 °C, 30 s @ 95 °C).

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data
steps.instruction: In the Agilent software, set the SYBR Green fluorescence threshold by locating the inflection point of the exponential phase and drawing a horizontal line. Record the Ct (dR) value at the intersection for each sample. Compute the mean Ct of the 5 % input control (biological triplicates). Calculate the G4RP‑RT‑qPCR signal as 5 × (2^(Mean Ct input) – Ct sample). For each target (e.g., NRAS, VEGFA) and each TASQ condition, average technical replicates, then average biological replicates. Plot the normalized signals and perform statistical tests as required.

description: G-quadruplexes (G4s)2 fold from guanine (G)-rich DNA3,4,5 and RNA6,7,8,9 sequences, which are highly abundant (> 1 million sequences) in the genome10 and transcriptome11 of human cells. The knowledge about G4 prevalence was acquired thanks to different techniques, either in silico12 or in vitro,13 the latter relying, for instance, either on polymerase stop assays (e.g., G4-seq for DNA G4,14 rG4-seq for RNA G4)15 or on the precipitation of G4s using ad hoc molecular tools (either antibodies,16,17,18,19,20 proteins21 or small molecules).22,23,24,25 Our contribution to this research effort was the development of the G4-RNA-specific precipitation (G4RP) protocol developed to identify RNA G4s that fold in in vivo conditions in human cancer cells. Two versions of this protocol were developed, depending on whether the analysis is targeted (G4RP-RT-qPCR)26 or transcriptome-wide (G4RP-seq).23,27 We report herein on a novel version of this protocol, named G4RP.v2, the key step of which is the specific precipitation of G4s using TASQs (for template-assembled synthetic G-quartets),28,29,30 a series of biomimetic ligands that display both high affinity and exquisite selectivity for G4s. The responsiveness of the G4RP.v2 protocol makes it suited to finely monitor the modulation of G4 landscapes in cells by chemical effectors (either G4 stabilizers31 or destabilizers)32; its reliability allows for asserting the G4 folding of PQS in a functional cellular context, often referred to as in vivo-like conditions given that cellular G4s are fixed prior to cell lysis and isolation (further detailed below); finally, its accuracy makes it ideally positioned to be used for the quantification of G4-containing genes expression in cancer cells. The protocol fully described below focuses on the application of G4RP.v2 for the accurate quantification by RT-qPCR of two G4-containing mRNAs, i.e., NRAS33 and VEGFA,34 as representative examples.
